Method of Attack: FluBot: uses smishing lures via SMS with fake courier messages, fake browser updates, fake voicemail notifications, and 'Is this you in this video?' coaxes; spreads by using infected device's contact list to send further SMS lures

TeaBot: distributed via trojanized apps on Google Play Store that appear legitimate; apps start background service checking country code, fetch configuration and APK from GitHub repository, prompt user to allow third-party app installation; apps promoted via Google Ads
Attack Vector: FluBot: SMS messages with social engineering lures
TeaBot: trojanized apps on Google Play Store
Indicators of Compromise: Over 100,000 malicious SMS intercepted since December 2021 (FluBot)

Trojanized apps on Google Play Store including QR Code Reader – Scanner App (100,000 downloads), QR Scanner APK (10,000 downloads), QR Code Scan (10,000 downloads), Smart Cleaner (1,000 downloads), Weather Cast (10,000 downloads), Weather Daily (10,000 downloads)
APK fetched from GitHub repository containing TeaBot variant
